title: Saints Pontian, Pope, and Hippolytus, Priest, Martyrs
short_summary: Saints Pontian and Hippolytus were third-century Romans, a pope and a priest-theologian, who were reconciled with one another and died in exile in the mines of Sardinia.
key_facts: The Church permits this optional memorial on August 13.
Pontian served as pope from 230 to 235.
Hippolytus was a priest and theologian of Rome who had been at odds with the Church of Rome for a time before his reconciliation.
Emperor Maximinus Thrax exiled both men to the mines of Sardinia, where conditions were harsh enough that the island was called the island of death.
Tradition holds that Pontian and Hippolytus were reconciled before their deaths in exile.

sections.heading: A pope who resigned under exile
sections.body: Pontian became bishop of Rome in 230. When Emperor Maximinus Thrax exiled him to the mines of Sardinia in 235, Pontian resigned his office so that the Roman church could elect a new pope, an early instance of a pope stepping down from office.

sections.heading: Hippolytus, priest and writer
sections.body: Hippolytus was a learned priest and prolific theological writer in Rome. For a period he had stood apart from the elected bishop of Rome, but he was reconciled with the Church before he too was condemned to exile in Sardinia.

sections.heading: Reconciliation before death
sections.body: Tradition holds that the two men were reconciled with one another in their shared exile and died there under the harsh conditions of the Sardinian mines. Their remains were later brought back to Rome and honored with a joint memorial.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Unity restored before death
catholic_connection_sections.body: The reconciliation of Pontian and Hippolytus points to the possibility of restored unity even after real division within the Church, when division gives way to humility and truth.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Faithfulness under suffering
catholic_connection_sections.body: Their deaths in exile join them to the wider company of early martyrs who suffered for the Christian faith in the mines and prisons of the Roman Empire.

historical_cautions: The precise circumstances of the reconciliation between Pontian and Hippolytus rest on early Christian tradition rather than a single detailed contemporary account, and are presented here with appropriate caution.
